info.name: EMS Pro API
info.description:
Every route the frontend calls, grouped by module, against a local `uvicorn app.main:app --reload` instance (see the repo README for setup).

**Auth**: the collection-level Bearer auth reads `{{access_token}}` from the environment. A test script on every request auto-captures `access_token` whenever a response body contains one (login, activation) — you never need to copy/paste it by hand.

**Run in this order for a first pass** (see the "Suggested order" folder for the exact requests):
1. `POST /companies/register` — creates a company in `pending` status.
2. Approve it as a `super_admin`. There is no self-serve way to get a `super_admin` account — Spec §8.5 deliberately makes that role assignable only by direct database action, never a route. Create one locally with:

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
from app.db.session import SessionLocal
from app.core.security import hash_password
from app.modules.identity.models import Company, CompanyStatus, User, UserRole

with SessionLocal() as db:
    company = Company(name="Platform Admin", code="PLATADMIN", email="platform@example.com", status=CompanyStatus.active)
    db.add(company)
    db.flush()
    db.add(User(company_id=company.id, email="admin@example.com",
                hashed_password=hash_password("ChangeMe123!"), role=UserRole.super_admin, is_active=True))
    db.commit()
EOF
```

   Then run `POST /auth/login` with that email/password, then `POST /companies/{company_id}/approve` (grab the id from the register response, or `GET /companies?status=pending`).
3. `POST /auth/login` again, this time as the `hr_admin` the approve step just created (its email/temp password come back in the approve response).
4. `POST /employees` to create an employee — the response includes an activation token; `POST /auth/activate` with it logs the new employee straight in.

Faster path for exploring everything else: skip steps 1-2 and run `scripts/seed_demo.py` (see README) for a company with 25 employees, attendance, leave and shifts already in every state, then just log in.

item.name: Auth & company onboarding

request.description: Route 1 (public). Creates the company in `pending` status. Note the returned `id` — you'll need it for the approve step.
super_admin only. Use to find the id of a company you just registered.
super_admin only. Creates the company's first hr_admin user and returns its email + a generated temporary password — copy both, you'll need them to log in as HR next.
super_admin only. Alternative to approve — left here for completeness, not part of the suggested order.

`company_code` is only needed if the same email exists at more than one company (rare — omit it normally). Sets a refresh-token cookie and returns an access token; the collection's test script captures the access token automatically.
Reads the refresh-token cookie Postman's cookie jar captured from Login — no body needed.
Revokes the current refresh token.
Revokes every refresh token issued to this user.
Returns the caller's role, company, linked employee summary and permission list.
Always returns the same message whether or not the email exists (Spec §9.3 enumeration safety) — check server logs / the OTP table locally to get the code, there's no email backend wired up in dev.
Public preview shown before an invited employee sets their password — 404 once expired or already redeemed.
Logs the employee straight in on success (Spec: no second login step) — response includes an access_token, auto-captured like Login.

hr_admin only. Copy the returned id into the `department_id` environment variable for the requests below.
Blocked (409) while any active employee is still assigned to it.
Scope depends on caller role (Spec §10.4): HR sees everyone, a manager sees their team, an employee sees only themself.

hr_admin only. Row stays in the database; deactivation just revokes login and drops the employee out of active lists (never a hard delete — Spec §10.1).

Poll with the job_id returned by an export endpoint (queued -> started -> success/failure).
